A game show offers you 4 identical doors: one hides a car, the other three hide goats. After you pick a door, the host, who knows what is behind each door, opens two of the remaining three doors, always revealing goats. Should you switch to the one remaining unopened door?
choices: No, staying is better since you chose first
Yes, but only because the host might be lying
No, both doors are equally likely (50/50)
Yes — switching gives a 3/4 chance of the car, versus 1/4 by staying

questions.q: Three light switches outside a windowless room each control one of three light bulbs inside. You may flip the switches however you like, but you may only enter the room ONE time. How can you determine with certainty which switch controls which bulb?
choices: It's impossible with only one entry
Turn on all three switches and enter immediately
Turn on switch A, wait, turn it off, turn on switch B, then enter — the lit bulb is B, the warm dark bulb is A, the cold dark bulb is C
Turn on switch A only, enter, then adjust based on brightness

questions.q: If the universe were infinite, static, and uniformly packed with stars, Olbers' Paradox asks why the night sky is mostly dark instead of uniformly bright. What is the standard modern resolution?
choices: The universe has a finite age, so light from the most distant stars hasn't reached us yet
The universe is infinite in age, so eventually the night sky will become bright
Dark matter absorbs all starlight before it reaches Earth
Stars block each other's light evenly, making the sky appear dark
